title: IFT-12 — Starship V3 Debut
description: 22 May 2026. First flight of Starship V3 (S39 / B19). One Raptor fails on ship — autonomous guidance extends burn 62 s to compensate. Booster lost in Gulf after boostback anomaly. Ship splashes down in Indian Ocean.
author: Markus Leutwyler

engineFailures._note: Raptor 5 on ship shuts down ~6 s after sep ignition; guidance extends burn autonomously

atcClearances.text: T minus 60 seconds. Starship is go for launch.
T minus 30 seconds.
Engine start sequence.
Liftoff. Starship lifts off from Starbase.
Max Q.
Super Heavy main engine cutoff.
Stage separation confirmed. Hot-staging nominal. Ship ignition.
We show an engine shutdown on Ship. Guidance is compensating — burn will extend.
Booster boostback burn has ended early. Tracking multiple engine anomalies on Booster 19.
Booster 19 — uncontrolled impact in the Gulf of Mexico. We will review the data.
Nominal SECO window open. Ship continuing to burn on five engines.
SECO confirmed. Ship reached target trajectory on five Raptors. Autonomous guidance performed nominally.
Payload bay open. Beginning Starlink simulator deployment.
Payload deployment complete. 22 simulators away.
Raptor engine relight confirmed. Ship performing on-orbit burn.
Ship entering the atmosphere over the Indian Ocean approach corridor.
Transonic.
Subsonic.
Landing burn start.
Splashdown confirmed. Ship 39 in the Indian Ocean.

narrative: One Raptor fails on Ship — guidance extends burn 62 seconds.
debrief: Did the engine failure callout come at T+2:30?
Did the ship reach SECO despite flying on 5 engines?
How much longer did the burn last compared to a nominal 6-engine flight?
What happened to Booster 19 in the Gulf?
